# Concave facet roofs: first variation controls affine cap discrepancy

This note is an ordinary planar calculation with a fixed concave roof.
It gives a functional stability identity, an actual convex-body
realization, and an explicit affine comparison. It is not a uniform
theorem for arbitrary changing roofs or for mixed-integer sources.

For a planar convex body K, mu_K is its normalized uniform area law,
and D(K)=max_(y in K) inf_(closed halfspaces H containing y) mu_K(H).
For two probability measures, dist_cap is the supremum over closed
halfspaces of the absolute difference of their masses. The notation
dist_cap(K, all affine triangles) is the infimum of
dist_cap(mu_K,mu_L) over all full-dimensional triangles L.

## 1. An exact functional deficit

Let psi:[0,1]->[0,infinity) be a continuous concave function, not
identically zero. Let I=[1/3,2/3], let ell(s)=a+bs be the affine
interpolant of psi at the endpoints of I, and define

    Z=int_0^1 psi(s)ds,
    E=int_I psi(s)ds-Z/3.

Concavity gives psi>=ell on I and psi<=ell outside I. The endpoint
inequalities ell(0)>=psi(0)>=0 and ell(1)>=psi(1)>=0 imply ell>=0
on the entire interval. Put

    A=int_I(psi-ell),
    B=int_([0,1] outside I)(ell-psi).

Since the integral of an affine function over I is exactly one third
of its integral over [0,1],

    E=(2A+B)/3>=0,
    int_0^1 |psi-ell|=A+B<=3E.                       (1)

In particular E=0 if and only if psi is affine. The continuity
assumption turns almost-everywhere equality into pointwise equality.
The inequality and the sign pattern are proved directly; no
unproved stability theorem for concave functions is invoked.

## 2. A convex body with this actual added-facet law

Use coordinates (s,r) in the plane and the area-one-half triangle

    T={0<=s<=1, s-1<=r<=0},  V=1/2.

The affine map (s,r)->(s,1-s+r) has determinant one and sends T to
the standard triangle. In these coordinates its barycentrics are
lambda_0=-r, lambda_1=s, lambda_2=1-s+r, and its centroid is
(1/3,-1/3).

For epsilon>0 let

    K_epsilon={0<=s<=1, s-1<=r<=epsilon psi(s)}.       (2)

This is a full-dimensional compact convex body: it lies between a
linear lower graph and a continuous concave upper graph on a compact
interval. It contains T, with exact added area epsilon Z. The uniform
probability law on the added strip converges weakly to the law on
r=0 with density psi(s)/Z. Indeed integration in r followed by uniform
continuity of a test function proves this directly. Its canonical
marginals have no mass on the centroid thresholds: lambda_0=0 is
away from 1/3, while lambda_1 and lambda_2 have densities.

The ordinary weak-added-law first-variation theorem proved in
candidate 7ff8cebaefda7361 applies.
On this facet the sum of the three canonical cap indicators is
one plus the indicator of I, outside null endpoints. It follows that
the NORMALIZED maximum depth satisfies

    D(K_epsilon)=4/9+epsilon E/(3V)+o(epsilon).       (3)

This is the maximum over all points and all halfspace directions,
not a computation at the original centroid. To check its coefficient,
the unnormalized first variation is epsilon(Z+int_I psi)/3;
dividing by V+epsilon Z subtracts (4/9)epsilon Z/V and gives (3).

## 3. One explicit affine triangle and the exact comparison costs

For epsilon small enough that 1-epsilon b>0, let

    L_epsilon={s>=0, s-1<=r<=epsilon ell(s)}.

It is an actual triangle with vertices

    (0,-1), (0,epsilon a), (s_*,s_*-1),
    s_*=(1+epsilon a)/(1-epsilon b)>=1.

The last inequality uses ell(1)=a+b>=0. On 0<=s<=1 the positive
part of K_epsilon outside L_epsilon has exact area epsilon A,
and the part of L_epsilon outside K_epsilon has area epsilon B.
Beyond s=1, L_epsilon has the additional triangular area

    J_epsilon=epsilon^2 ell(1)^2/[2(1-epsilon b)].   (4)

Thus the complete difference and area identities are

    |K outside L|=epsilon A,
    |L outside K|=epsilon B+J_epsilon,
    |K|=V+epsilon Z,
    |L|=(1+epsilon a)^2/[2(1-epsilon b)].             (5)

For normalized uniform laws on any two finite positive-volume sets,
total variation equals one minus intersection volume divided by the
larger total volume. Applying that exact identity to (5) gives

    TV(mu_K,mu_L)
       =max(epsilon A,epsilon B+J_epsilon)
                      /max(|K|,|L|).

In particular

    lim_(epsilon->0) TV(mu_K,mu_L)/epsilon
        =max(A,B)/V<=3E/V.                          (6)

The closed-halfspace cap distance is at most total variation. Since
L_epsilon is an admissible affine triangle comparison, (3) and (6)
show, whenever E>0, that

    liminf_(epsilon->0)
       [D(K_epsilon)-4/9]
          /dist_cap(K_epsilon, all affine triangles) >=1/9,     (7)

with a zero denominator interpreted as no obstacle to the lower bound.
Equivalently, for every fixed constant c<1/9 and this fixed roof,
the inequality with coefficient c holds for all sufficiently small
epsilon. The threshold may depend on psi; no uniform relative
remainder is claimed when roofs vary and E tends to zero.

## 4. The affine zero-deficit case has an exact second-order model

If E=0, psi=ell is affine. Then K_epsilon is L_epsilon cut by s<=1.
If ell(1)=0, s_*=1 and it is itself a triangle. Otherwise the deleted
piece is a corner homothetic to L_epsilon, of relative area

    tau_epsilon=[epsilon ell(1)/(1+epsilon a)]^2.     (8)

Both incident cut fractions tend to zero, so the theorem in
candidate 3795aff5f3322d52
applies. It gives

    D(K_epsilon)
      =[2(1+sqrt(1+3tau_epsilon))/9
                         -2tau_epsilon/3]/(1-tau_epsilon),
    D(K_epsilon)-4/9=tau_epsilon/9+O(tau_epsilon^2). (9)

Here dist_cap(mu_K,mu_L)=tau_epsilon exactly, since the deleted
corner is a halfspace trace with no K area. Thus the vanishing
first variation in (3) reflects an affine first-order motion;
the remaining cap discrepancy and depth excess both have order
epsilon^2. This explains that cancellation without treating a
first-order zero as a counterexample to cap-distance stability.

No optimal affine comparison or minimizing triangle is assumed to
exist in this argument: the displayed L_epsilon supplies every
comparison used. All measures are ordinary planar area, and all
closed halfspace boundaries have zero area. The only limiting depth
theorem used has been separately proved and independently audited.
